data.analysis: Choose N=3: the source and measurements support three complementary opportunities in this one-kernel O(N²) workload—reuse source particles across target rows, increase parallelism within each target row, and reduce per-interaction arithmetic. The first two are distinct execution mappings; the third can be tested independently and combined later. The supplied baseline is valid and correct, with three reported search times averaging 0.00185514 s; per-size timings and independent confirmation are not provided, so this is a baseline rather than evidence for any optimization. The target and interface are specified as one GH200, NVRTC CUDA 12.6.3, fixed Particle layout and entry point, and limited launch configuration. CUDA documentation consulted was the publisher-current CUDA Best Practices Guide 13.4, not version-matched to the target; it supports only general memory-hierarchy and floating-point-rounding considerations, not a target-specific performance claim.

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, investigate a single-kernel strategy that stages source Particle tiles in shared memory and reuses them across multiple target rows, keeping the main mapping one thread per target rather than parallelizing a row reduction. Tune viable tile sizes, loading/layout choices, and the permitted launch.json parameters. Preserve the entry point, 28-byte Particle layout, complete output state, self-interaction handling, arbitrary-N tail coverage, and the one-kernel/no-host-preprocessing constraint. Validate every candidate against the full prescribed correctness checks, then compare measured geometric-mean event time across the three scored sizes; retain slower or incorrect attempts in the tree evidence.
children.subject: Shared-memory source tiling across target rows

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, investigate a distinct mapping in which warps or CTAs cooperate over the source-particle j dimension for each target row, reduce the force components, and use the permitted launch configuration to expose sufficient parallel work on the GH200. Focus on row-parallelism and reduction rather than cross-target source tiling as the primary innovation; local storage or synchronization needed for the reduction is acceptable. Cover every j exactly once, handle self-interactions and tails for all N, preserve the fixed interface and one-kernel constraint, and validate against the full prescribed checks before comparing scored-size geometric-mean event time.
children.subject: Cooperative source-parallel force accumulation

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, explore algebraically equivalent float32 interaction formulas that reduce expensive math operations, such as selective reciprocal-square-root use and cancellation of the target mass between force accumulation and acceleration. Do not enable global fast math or assume benchmark-specific inputs. Preserve safe self-interaction handling, all supported dt values, finite outputs, exact mass copies, and the required reference tolerance across the independent correctness data, including extreme-mass coverage. Measure correctness-valid candidates and their scored-size geometric-mean event times; record failures and regressions.
children.subject: Float32 interaction arithmetic simplification
